newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude erases most of Iraq-led rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude erases most of Iraq-led rally.

text.p: IPE Brent crude shed most of the session's gains later on Tuesday as dealers took profits after a sharp rally driven by U.S. air strikes against Iraq.
By 1419 GMT, Oct Brent was up 16 cents at $22.15 a barrel, more than 60 cents off the high.
"It's the normal ebb and flow of an overnight story... it's very choppy," said a broker.

A U.S. missile attack early Tuesday against air defence targets in southern Iraq sparked the rally, but prices pulled back when Iraq said it would withdraw completely from Kurdish regions in the north.
Dealers said Brent crude was under pressure from weaker than expected follow-through gains in New York.
"NYMEX opened roughly where expected but it's come off since then," said a broker.
Brent -- which remains more than $1 a barrel up since Friday -- continued to draw support from the weekend's postonement of the U.N.'s May 20 oil-for-food deal with Iraq.

The U.S. envoy to the U.N. Edward Gnehm said on Tuesday that the accord, agreed after months of laborious negotiations, needs to be reopened in the wake of military action by Baghdad in the north of the country, which prompted the U.S. strike.
Gnehm said he could not offer an estimate on how long implementation of the oil-for-food deal is likely to remain on hold, saying that would be decided by Saddam Hussein's actions.
"It could be months and months," he said.
Oil analysts and traders said Baghdad's latest military adventure has probably derailed plans for the resumption of Iraqi exports beyond the end of the year.
The U.N. deal, allowed Bahgdad $2 billion of oil sales renewable every six months, worth about 550,000 barrels per day (bpd) at last week's prices.
